items.title: LG enters chip packaging arena with Laser Direct Imaging machine, as TSMC's CoWoS remains constrained — maskless machine is designed to pattern fine interconnects, trading resolution for higher throughput
items.description: LG rolls-out laser direct imaging lithography machine for chip packaging and high-density PCBs.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter As advanced packaging technologies like EMIB and CoWoS become yet another battlefield in the semiconductor industry, outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) companies are trying new tools in a bid to offer services that others do not. This week, LG Electronics Production Technology Institute (PRI) signed a contract with an OSAT to supply it with a maskless laser direct imaging (LDI) lithography tool that can be used to build metal-interconnect patterns in semiconductor packaging, potentially with higher yields than currently available tools, reports ETNews.LG-PRI's Laser Direct Imaging (LDI) system is a maskless lithography machine designed to pattern fine metal interconnects for advanced semiconductor packaging. While the company has developed various versions of the machine, its highest-resolution version can produce 1.5-µm line-and-space (L/S) patterns, which should be fine to 'print' wiring pitches of about 3 µm. The production equipment uses a 405-nm laser-diode light source and can process substrates as large as 600 × 600 mm, according to various media reports.LG positions its LDI system primarily for advanced semiconductor packaging using organic and then glass substrates, displays, and MEMS. Yet, it can also be used to build high-density printed circuit boards (PCBs) for mobile devices or prototype purposes.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: LG is entering an already established direct-imaging market led by KLA, Screen Holdings, Limata, and ORC, but participated in by a dozen manufacturers from Germany, France, Switzerland, Japan, and even China. What is notable is that LG is offering LDI systems with line/space capability down to 1.5-µm, which means it is targeting the higher end of the market. Yet, to establish a position, LG plans to price its LDI system competitively.Another way to pattern substratesThere are many ways to pattern substrates, including photolithography, e-beam lithography, nanoimprint lithography, and laser direct imaging, just to name a few. LDI is a maskless lithography process in which a laser exposes a digitally generated circuit pattern directly onto a photoresist-coated substrate, rather than transferring the pattern through a physical photomask. Instead of a photomask, an LDI system uses a digitally controlled pattern generator and projection optics, which resembles how a laser cinema projector projects a digital image onto a screen, except that LDI projects a circuit pattern onto photoresist. After development, the exposed resist leaves a pattern that defines where metal interconnects will be formed in later processing steps. You may like Intel's EMIB packaging gains traction as chip designers look beyond TSMC's constrained CoWoS TSMC says panel packaging won't replace CoWoS anytime soon for the largest future AI processors Chinese startup claims photonic chip production without DUV lithography, says nanoimprint process cuts costs by 90% (Image credit: LG)LG's LDI machine can produce down to 1.5-µm line-and-space patterns, which is good enough for chip substrates and even redistribution layers (TSMC CoWoS-R/-L uses RDL interposers with a minimum 4-µm pitch, or 2-µm line width/spacing). In contrast, competing products offer 1-µm, 3-µm, and 5-µm versions for different applications. While LDI in general cannot boast the resolutions offered by modern DUV, EUV, or e-beam lithography machines, LDI trades ultimate resolution for vastly higher throughput and large-area processing, exactly what the doctor ordered for production of PCBs or chip packaging. With current-generation LDI, the RDL interposer is the most advanced thing that these devices can pattern, as both CoWoS-S and CoWoS-L/EMIB-like technologies require considerably higher resolution. Meanwhile, there is another advantage that LDI machines have over lithography systems that rely on photomasks.Because the image is generated digitally, the system can create and calibrate patterns in real time, while projection optics, precision alignment, and stage control position the pattern accurately on the substrate. This capability is important because the dimensions/geometry of packaging substrates can vary and because organic substrates can expand, contract, or warp during processing. Given that we are talking about a 1.5-µm-scale wiring pattern, any shift from the nominal layout may result in a solder bridge or a faulty contact, which means yield loss. That said, the ability to adjust the pattern to the peculiarities of a substrate may be a game-changer for OSATs, their customers, and a major selling point for devices that can do it.A new kid on the block? Not reallyUnlike competing chaebols Samsung and SK Group, LG Group does not produce chips, even though its divisions supply various materials and components for the semiconductor industry. To that end, it is perfectly reasonable for the company to enter the market for tools for the production of chip packages or PCBs.In fact, LG PRI is not entering the exposure-equipment business from scratch. PRI traces its history to the Goldstar Production Technology Research Institute, established in 1987, and has worked on manufacturing and productivity technologies covering semiconductors, displays, and rechargeable batteries. Specifically, LG had already commercialized LDI technology for display manufacturing and supplied such equipment to LG Display.As a result, the semiconductor packaging-grade equipment represents an expansion of an existing LG technology into a new market rather than the development of an entirely new exposure platform from scratch and without any experience. Interestingly, LDI is the first element of LG's semiconductor equipment ambitions. The company reportedly plans to expand its portfolio into high-bandwidth memory (HBM) inspection equipment as well as through-glass-via (TGV) laser systems for glass substrates.ProspectsBefore LG expands to inspection or laser drilling tools, it will have to establish itself as a producer of reliable tools used for chip packaging, which will likely take years. For now, the significance of the deal with the undisclosed OSAT is less about business and more about the fact that an OSAT decided to give LG's LDI machine a try. Moving from university R&D installations to an OSAT mass-production facility provides LG a starting point for pursuing additional external orders.Whether LG can establish itself alongside Applied Materials, ORC, or Screen will depend on how its equipment performs in production and whether its emphasis on competitive pricing proves sufficient to persuade more packaging companies to adopt the system.In any case, a new Wafer Fab Equipment player is here, which is good news considering shortages of virtually all chipmaking tools. While LG's entrance will hardly have any noticeable impact on the market for at least a couple of years, another supplier could eventually add much-needed capacity, increase competition, and give chipmakers and OSATs another source of advanced packaging equipment.

items.titleZh: LG enters chip packaging arena with Laser Direct Imaging machine, as TSMC's CoWoS remains constrained — maskless machine is designed to pattern fine interconnects, trading resolution for higher throughput
items.descriptionZh:
先进封装技术正成为半导体产业竞争的新战场。随着英特尔的EMIB和台积电的CoWoS等先进封装方案日益普及，委外封装测试（OSAT）厂商正在积极寻找差异化工具，以提供别家没有的服务。本周，LG电子生产技术研究院（PRI）与一家OSAT签署合同，将向其供应一台无掩模激光直接成像（LDI）光刻设备，用于在半导体封装中制作金属互连图案，并有望比现有设备实现更高良率。

LG PRI的LDI系统是一种无掩模光刻设备，专为先进半导体封装精细金属互连图案化而设计。该公司开发了多个版本，其中最高分辨率版本可产生1.5微米的线宽/间距（L/S）图形，足以“印刷”约3微米间距的布线。该生产设备采用405纳米激光二极管光源，可处理最大600×600毫米的基板。LG将该系统主要定位用于基于有机基板、未来将扩展至玻璃基板的先进封装，以及显示器和MEMS领域，同时也可用于制造高密度移动设备PCB或原型样品。

LDI是一种无掩模光刻工艺：激光器将数字生成的电路图形直接投射到涂有光刻胶的基板上，而无需通过物理光掩模转印图案。它采用数字控制的图形发生器与投影光学元件，工作原理类似于激光影院投影仪将数字图像投射到屏幕上，只不过LDI投射的是电路图形到光刻胶上。显影后，光刻胶留下的图案定义了后续金属互连的形成位置。由于图像是数字生成的，系统可实时创建和校准图形，同时通过投影光学、精密对准和载台控制将图案准确位置于基板上。这一能力至关重要，因为封装基板的尺寸/几何形状可能变化，且有机基板在加工过程中会膨胀、收缩或翘曲。当涉及1.5微米级布线图案时，任何与名义布局的偏移都可能导致焊桥或接触不良，造成良率损失。因此，根据基板特性调整图案的能力可能成为OSAT及其客户的游戏规则改变者，也是具备此功能设备的一大卖点。

就分辨率而言，LDI无法与现代DUV、EUV或电子束光刻机相提并论，但它的取舍在于以极限分辨率为代价换取极高的生产效率和大幅面处理能力，这正是PCB或芯片封装生产所需要的。然而，LDI设备的另一个优势是：它可以不需要光掩模，直接数字生成并校准图形，还能适应基板的形变，这对先进封装尤其有价值。就当前代LDI而言，RDL中介层是这类设备能图案化的最先进产品——因为CoWoS-S和CoWoS-L/EMIB类技术需要高得多的分辨率。但LG的1.5微米L/S能力足以应对芯片基板甚至再分布层（TSMC CoWoS-R/-L采用最小4微米间距，即2微米线宽/间距的RDL中介层）。相比之下，竞争对手提供1微米、3微米和5微米版本以适应不同应用。

LG进入的是一个已由KLA、Screen Holdings、Limata和ORC主导的直接成像市场，参与者还包括来自德国、法国、瑞士、日本乃至中国的十余家制造商。值得关注的是，LG提供线宽/间距低至1.5微米的LDI系统，表明其瞄准市场高端。但为了建立地位，LG计划将LDI系统定在具有竞争力的价格。该技术的核心卖点之一是能处理有机基板在加工中的膨胀、收缩和翘曲，因为LDI可动态调整图案，避免因基板变形导致的良率损失。

LG集团与竞争对手三星、SK集团不同，不生产芯片，但其部门为半导体行业供应各种材料和组件。因此，进入芯片封装或PCB生产设备市场是完全合理的。事实上，LG PRI并非从零起步进入曝光设备领域。PRI的历史可追溯至1987年成立的金星生产技术研究院，长期研究涵盖半导体、显示器和可充电电池的生产与制造技术。具体而言，LG此前已将LDI技术商业化用于显示制造，并向LG Display供应此类设备。因此，半导体封装级设备是LG既有技术向新市场的扩展，而非毫无经验地开发全新曝光平台。有趣的是，LDI是LG半导体设备雄心的第一步，据报道该公司计划将产品组合扩展至高带宽内存（HBM）检测设备以及用于玻璃基板的玻璃通孔（TGV）激光系统。

在LG扩展到检测或激光钻孔工具之前，它必须首先确立自己作为可靠的芯片封装工具生产商的地位，这可能需要数年时间。目前，与未具名OSAT达成的协议，其意义与其说在于商业层面，不如说在于一家OSAT决定试用LG的LDI设备。从大学研发装置走向OSAT量产工厂，为LG提供了争取更多外部订单的起点。LG能否在应用材料（Applied Materials）、ORC或Screen等厂商面前立足，取决于其设备在生产中的表现，以及其强调的有竞争力的定价是否足以说服更多封装企业采用该系统。无论如何，一家新的晶圆厂设备（WFE）参与者出现了——考虑到几乎所有芯片制造工具都短缺，这无疑是好消息。尽管LG的进入在至少两年内不会对市场产生明显影响，但最终，新的供应商可能增加急需的产能、提升竞争，并为芯片制造商和OSAT提供另一个先进封装设备来源。事实上，这篇文章本身来自Tom's Hardware，其中还提到Intel的EMIB封装正在获得更多关注，而TSMC的CoWoS产能受限，以及一家中国初创公司声称无需DUV光刻即可生产光子芯片等等，这些都构成了先进封装设备需求旺盛的背景。LG的LDI设备以其1.5微米L/S能力、数字无掩模技术、实时校准和适应基板变形的能力，为高端封装市场带来了新选择，同时其竞争性定价策略和从显示器LDI延伸而来的技术积累，使其在市场中具有潜力。未来能否在先进封装设备领域站稳脚跟，将取决于实际量产表现和客户接受度。

items.title: Supermicro fires several employees following investigation into $2.5 billion China AI chip smuggling — claims that senior management had no knowledge of illicit transactions
items.description: An independent investigation on Supermicro clears senior management from any wrong-doing and also says that its financial statements were still reliable, despite the alleged diversion of its restricted products. Nevertheless, some of its employees from sales, technical support, and business development departments were fired for failing to 'follow Company policies or the Company’s code of conduct.'
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Five months after the arrest of Supermicro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw and two other co-conspirators for the alleged smuggling of Nvidia hardware into China, the company announced that it has completed its independent investigation and released its findings to the public, resulting in the termination of several employees. Supermicro said that the investigation, which was handled by an external law firm and conducted by an “independent forensic accounting consultant,” finds that neither the company nor its current senior executives were part of the alleged AI chip smuggling. It also said that it’s adopting all the recommendations to enhance its export compliance programs, although it did not directly admit that it was lacking in that department.Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explained“The investigation team reviewed the customer transactions that were the subject of the federal indictment, as well as transactions with a selection of other customers who bought restricted products, and did not find any evidence that any current member of senior management had knowledge of the alleged diversion scheme or of any actual diversion of restricted products by the Company,” Supermicro said in the statement. It also added, “The Company’s compliance personnel have acted in good faith, with the support of management, to mitigate the risk of the Company’s products subject to export controls being diverted to restricted parties or locations.”This odyssey began in March when the U.S. charged Liaw alongside Supermicro sales manager Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang and third-party broker Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun with conspiracy to unlawfully divert cutting-edge U.S. artificial intelligence technology to China. The accused aren’t operating a small-time smuggling operation, either — reports estimate that the three have smuggled hardware worth $2.5 billion since 2024. That massive amount has got shareholders worried that a huge chunk of the company’s sales come from illicit sales, resulting in some investors suing the company for securities fraud. Because of this, the company’s independent advisors also looked into this issue and said that it “did not find any evidence that the Company’s previously issued financial statements could not be relied upon based on the potential diversion of restricted products.”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Even though the third-party investigation exonerated Supermicro’s senior executives, it also resulted in the termination of several employees. The affected people were from the sales, technical support, and business development departments, although they were fired for breaking the company’s policies and code of conduct — the company said these moves were made "in connection with the investigation." Notably, none of the personnel were from its compliance department, and it’s also unclear how many people were dismissed.Supermicro also said that it’s enhancing its export compliance program, which Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said it must fix. Even though the company was never accused of wrongdoing and wasn’t part of the defendants in the case against the alleged smugglers, the fact that some of its employees were able to run a massive diversion scheme right within the organization raises major questions about the effectiveness of its compliance department. It said that it has already made changes that were recommended by its General Counsel and Chief Compliance Officer even before the third-party investigation concluded, and that its independent directors “will oversee implementation of the remaining recommendations.” You may like After $2.5 billion Supermicro smuggling bust, Nvidia CEO urges company to fix export control compliance Supermicro says it assisted Taiwanese authorities in server smuggling bust that led to three arrests Nvidia employee implicated in escalating AI GPU smuggling scandal The high demand for AI chips in China has meant the smuggling operations are quite lucrative, even as the U.S. is tightening its grip on export controls and Chinese authorities are commanding that its tech companies prioritize locally made Chinese chips instead of American AI GPUs. Nevertheless, the race to build ever more powerful AI models means that there is such a massive demand for the most advanced AI GPUs from Nvidia that some people are looking for ways to circumvent these bans and make “easy” money. items.titleZh: Supermicro fires several employees following investigation into $2.5 billion China AI chip smuggling — claims that senior management had no knowledge of illicit transactions
items.descriptionZh:
在Supermicro联合创始人Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw 与另外两名同伙因涉嫌向中国走私Nvidia硬件而被捕五个月后，该公司正式宣布其独立调查已告完成，并公开了调查结果。此次调查由外部律师事务所主导，并由独立法务会计顾问具体执行。Supermicro在声明中强调，调查未发现公司或其现任高级管理人员参与了这起所谓的AI芯片走私案，同时表示将采纳所有建议以强化出口合规计划，尽管并未直接承认此前在合规方面存在不足。

这起事件的源头可追溯至今年3月，美国司法部对Liaw、Supermicro销售经理Ruei-Tsang "Steven" Chang以及第三方中介Ting-Wei "Willy" Sun提起指控，罪名是共谋将美国尖端人工智能技术非法转移至中国。值得注意的是，这并非小规模的地下走私——据估算，自2024年以来，三人所走私的硬件总价值高达25亿美元。这一惊人金额引发了股东对该公司大量销售可能源于非法交易的担忧，进而导致部分投资者以证券欺诈为由将公司告上法庭。为此，公司独立顾问也对此进行了审查，并明确表示“未发现任何证据表明，基于受限产品潜在转移问题，公司此前发布的财务报表不可信赖”。

调查团队重点审查了联邦起诉书所涉的客户交易，以及一批购买受限产品的其他客户交易记录。Supermicro在声明中指出，调查未发现任何现任高级管理人员知晓所谓“转移计划”或公司实际将受限产品转移他处的证据。同时，公司合规人员在管理层的支持下一直秉持善意行事，以降低出口管制产品被转移到受限方或受限地点的风险。

尽管第三方调查为高管层洗清了嫌疑，但调查结果仍导致多名员工被解雇。这些被解雇人员来自销售、技术支持及业务发展部门，原因是违反公司政策和行为准则，公司称此举与“调查相关”。值得注意的是，被解雇人员中没有一名来自合规部门，且公司未透露具体解雇人数。Supermicro还表示正在加强出口合规计划——而这一点正是Nvidia首席执行官黄仁勋此前明确要求其必须修复的。尽管Supermicro本身从未被指控有不当行为，也未在该走私案中被列为被告，但员工能在组织内部运作如此大规模的转移计划，已经让外界对其合规部门实际效力产生了重大质疑。公司透露，早在第三方调查结束前，总法律顾问和首席合规官所建议的部分改革措施已开始实施，独立董事也将负责监督其余建议的落实。

这一事件折射出更宏观的行业背景：中国对AI芯片的需求极其旺盛，尽管美国不断收紧出口管制，且中国官方强制要求国内科技公司优先采购本土芯片而非美国AI GPU，但快速迭代的大模型竞赛使得最先进的Nvidia AI GPU仍然存在巨大缺口，这为走私者提供了绕开禁令牟取暴利的空间。此次调查虽然为Supermicro高管层化解了法律风险，但如何真正堵住合规漏洞，仍是这家服务器制造商乃至整个行业必须面对的长期挑战。

items.title: H200 AI GPUs finally reach China under case-by-case import licenses, but it's already too late for Nvidia — homemade chips corner the China market as country seeks semiconductor independence
items.description: Most of each company's U.S.-licensed allowance, understood to be up to 100,000 units apiece, must stay outside the mainland.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter ByteDance and Tencent each took delivery of roughly 10,000 Nvidia H200 accelerators in recent weeks, and a handful of other Chinese tech groups may soon receive approvals of similar size. The deliveries are the first meaningful movement of the chips into mainland China since President Trump cleared their export in December, but they arrive under strict oversight from China’s National Development and Reform Commission, which approves each purchase individually.Most of each company's U.S.-licensed allowance, understood to be up to 100,000 units apiece, must stay outside the mainland, largely in Hong Kong. Measured against the 400,000-plus units that ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent were collectively approved to buy in January, the chips now on the mainland amount to roughly 2.5% of the order book.Two licensing regimesTrump approved H200 exports in December last year, in exchange for a 25% cut of every sale to the U.S. Treasury, and terms formalized in January require each chip to pass through US territory for third-party inspection before re-export. The Commerce Department moved license applications to case-by-case review on January 16 and had cleared roughly 10 firms by mid-May, including Alibaba, ByteDance, Tencent, and JD.com, with Lenovo and Foxconn approved as distributors.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: In response, China built the NDRC’s per-purchase approval process from scratch to mirror the Commerce Department’s case-by-case license review. The 10,000-unit mainland allocations function as quantity caps, the very instrument that U.S. export rules have used since the first Hopper restrictions in 2022. The requirement to route imports via Hong Kong operates as an end-location condition, identical to Washington's demand that every chip transit U.S. soil for inspection.The Cyberspace Administration of China summoned Nvidia last July over alleged backdoors in the H20. State media outlets subsequently ran a campaign calling the chip unsafe and outdated, and state-funded data centers were barred from foreign accelerators. Eight months of NDRC silence on H200 orders left Jensen Huang telling investors Nvidia's China market share had gone from 95% to zero. You may like First Nvidia H200 shipments reach China, ByteDance and Tencent take deliveries as Beijing loosens its import block US allows Chinese telecom giant ZTE to purchase Nvidia H200 AI chips US closes loophole that allowed Chinese-owned subsidiaries located outside China to buy AI chips DeepSeek’s training bottleneckA transcript of DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng's May 20 closed-door investor meeting, leaked online in July, arguably explains why Beijing is letting any Nvidia silicon in at all. According to the document, whose authenticity DeepSeek hasn't confirmed, Liang told investors he wanted 200,000 Huawei accelerators to train a frontier model and received an allocation of 16,000, against total Huawei capacity of roughly 750,000 chips this year split across every Chinese AI company, a constraint he reportedly expected to persist for around three years. The remarks circulated widely enough that DeepSeek paused a fundraising round targeting a roughly $71 billion valuation days after they appeared.If we look at DeepSeek’s production history, it appears to match the numbers Liang cited during the meeting. lab's attempts to train its R2 model on Huawei Ascend hardware failed repeatedly, and training moved back to Nvidia chips while Ascend accelerators handle inference. Per the Financial Times’ unnamed source, which broke the story of resuming H200 imports, domestic silicon increasingly serves inference, while Nvidia hardware still carries training.The H200 obviously fills that gap nicely, with each unit carrying 141GB of HBM3e at 4.8 TB/s, delivering roughly six times the performance of the H20, and approaching the banned H100. A 10,000-GPU cluster is genuine frontier-training capacity, comparable to the builds behind the GPT-4 generation, though it represents a fraction of the 100,000-GPU-plus systems U.S. labs now run. That ratio seems to have been precisely calibrated by Beijing officials, large enough to keep flagship labs training their models, but small enough that inference stays a captive market for domestic chipmakers.Domestic supply gapsTrendForce's August 10 supply chain survey projects that domestic chips will take nearly 90% of China's high-end AI chip market this year, with domestic high-end shipments growing 83% year over year, a projection that TrendForce itself revised up from roughly 50% in its December outlook. Bernstein has recorded the same displacement from the other direction, with Nvidia's China share falling from 66% in 2024 to 40% in 2025 and a projected 8% this year.Huawei planned to roughly double output of its 910C Ascend chip to about 600,000 units in 2026, against a total Chinese accelerator market that ran to roughly 4 million units in 2025, 2.36 million of them supplied by Nvidia and AMD. So, while domestic chips can cover the volume, they can't yet cover frontier training, making the 90% projection and H200 easing two halves of the same policy.Washington's case for export controls rests on exactly the dependence these deliveries demonstrate: Four years into the restrictions, China's leading labs still can't train frontier models without American silicon, and Beijing has now conceded as much through its licensing decision.The leaked transcript has Liang arguing that open access to Nvidia would make domestic substitution a much harder commercial proposition, meaning the controls themselves built the market Huawei and Cambricon now hold, and TrendForce's numbers show that market approaching 90% share three years after the first Hopper bans. This month's deliveries disprove neither side's theory, but Nvidia does bear the cost of both, with 500,000 chips reportedly in inventory, a 25% fee on anything that sells, and a Chinese market rationed to 10,000 units per buyer — admittedly, that’s better than zero.
items.author: Luke James
items.titleZh: H200 AI GPU终于通过逐案进口许可进入中国，但对英伟达来说已为时过晚——随着中国寻求半导体独立，国产芯片已抢占中国市场
items.descriptionZh:
字节跳动与腾讯近日各收到约1万块英伟达H200加速器，这是自去年12月特朗普政府批准该芯片对华出口以来，首批大规模进入中国大陆的英伟达高端AI芯片。据悉，阿里、京东等中国科技集团也可能很快获得类似规模的审批。每家公司获批的芯片总量上限据称可达10万块，但绝大多数必须存放于境外（主要是香港），真正进入大陆的配额仅为总量的约四分之一。与今年1月字节跳动、阿里、腾讯合计获批的40余万块订单相比，此次实际交付仅占订单量的约2.5%。

这批芯片的放行背后是中美两套高度对称的许可制度。美方出口条件包括：每笔销售需向美国财政部缴纳25%的提成，且每颗芯片必须过境美国本土接受第三方检查后方可转口；商务部自1月16日起改为逐案审查，已在5月中旬前批准约10家企业，联想和富士康则获批为分销商。作为回应，中国发改委从零搭建了逐笔采购审批流程，将1万块大陆配额作为数量上限，并强制要求经香港转运，这恰好对应了美国自2022年首轮Hopper限制以来惯用的数量管控与终端位置条款。

此前，中国对英伟达芯片的态度一度十分严厉。去年7月，国家网信办曾就H20芯片涉嫌存在后门召见英伟达，官媒随后发起宣传攻势称该芯片不安全且过时，国有数据中心被明令禁止采购外国加速器。发改委对H200订单长达八个月的沉默，曾让黄仁勋向投资者坦言，英伟达在中国市场的份额已从95%降至零。

此次政策转向的直接动因，很可能是中国头部AI实验室在国产芯片上的训练困境。一份据称是DeepSeek创始人梁文锋5月20日闭门投资者会议的纪要（真实性未获官方确认）显示，他曾申请20万块华为昇腾加速器用于训练前沿模型，实际仅获得1.6万块的配额——华为当年的总产能约75万块，需分配给所有中国AI公司，这一瓶颈预计将持续三年。该纪要流传后，DeepSeek一度暂停了估值约710亿美元的融资。从DeepSeek的生产实践来看，其R2模型在昇腾硬件上多次训练失败，不得不转回英伟达芯片，昇腾仅承担推理任务，这与外媒“国产芯片主推理、英伟达主训练”的报道相吻合。

H200恰好填补了这一空缺。每块H200配备141GB HBM3e高带宽内存，带宽达4.8TB/s，性能约为此前特供中国的H20的六倍，接近被禁的H100。一个由1万块H200组成的集群，已具备训练GPT-4一代模型的真实前沿算力，但与美国实验室普遍拥有的10万卡级系统相比仍有量级差距。这一比例显然是北京方面精算的结果：足以让头部实验室继续训练模型，又不足以让推理市场脱离国产芯片的“圈养”，从而为华为昇腾、寒武纪等本土厂商保留核心市场空间。

TrendForce于8月10日发布的供应链调查预计，国产芯片今年将占据中国高端AI芯片市场近90%的份额，高端出货量同比增长83%——该机构已在去年12月约50%的预测基础上大幅上调。Bernstein的数据从另一角度印证了同样的趋势：英伟达在华份额已从2024年的66%降至2025年的40%，预计今年仅剩8%。华为计划在2026年将其910C昇腾芯片产量翻倍至约60万块；而2025年中国加速器市场总量约400万块，其中236万块来自英伟达和AMD。数字表明，国产芯片虽可覆盖规模需求，却仍无法支撑前沿训练，90%的国产化预测与H200的有限放行，本质上是同一政策的两面。

华盛顿坚持出口管制的理由，恰好被这批交付所证实：限制实施四年后，中国顶尖实验室依然离不开美国芯片来训练前沿模型，北京通过许可决定承认了这一点。而泄露的纪要中梁文锋的观点则指出了另一面——若无美国芯片的开放供应，国产替代的商业动力将大幅削弱，正是出口管制“帮助”华为和寒武纪建立了今天的市场。TrendForce的数据显示，管制三年后国产份额已逼近90%，也印证了这一逻辑。本月这批交付无法最终裁决谁的理论更正确，但英伟达显然为此付出双重代价：据传其积压库存达50万块，任何在售芯片都要上交25%的利润，而中国大陆市场被限额在每个买家1万块——不过，对英伟达来说，这终究好过销量为零。

items.title: Nvidia denies report it will ship Groq-based LPUs to China by year-end — says there is 'no China-specific LPU product in our roadmap'
items.description: Nvidia has rejected a report published by The Information that it plans to begin small-batch shipments of an LPU tailored for Chinese customers by the end of 2026.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia has rejected a report claiming that it plans to begin small-batch shipments of a language processing unit tailored for Chinese customers by the end of 2026, with several Chinese orders already placed. "The reporting in The Information on NVIDIA's LPU is incorrect. We have no LPU sales in the China market today, and no China-specific LPU product in our roadmap," an Nvidia spokesperson told Tom's Hardware on Thursday. The Information's story, which cited two Nvidia employees, said the chip is a variant of the Groq 3 LPU Nvidia announced at GTC in March, and that its silicon is unchanged because it already falls within U.S. export rules.Tom's Hardware Premium Roadmaps (Image credit: Future)Leading-edge foundry roadmapsNvidia Enterprise GPU and CPU roadmapAMD's Enterprise GPU and CPU roadmapIntel's roadmaps examined — 14A, Nova Lake, Diamond Rapids & AI accelerator pushCo-Packaged Optics (CPO) foundry roadmapsThe LPU was designed as a decode co-processor for the Vera Rubin platform, and Vera Rubin can't be sold in China. The Information's sources said Nvidia rewrote the software that splits work between the GPU and the LPU so the accelerator can run alongside processors that are available in the country.The publication said Nvidia didn't respond to requests for comment over several days before publishing, and that it's unclear whether Beijing would allow the orders to proceed. Chinese officials blocked purchases of the H20 last year and only recently told companies they'd permit some H200 imports, so U.S. compliance alone doesn't guarantee the chips can be delivered.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Back in March, it was reported that Nvidia was preparing LPUs for China, with Jensen Huang saying two days later that the story was "totally false.” Thursday's statement is narrower than Huang's, addressing current sales and a China-specific product. Nvidia hasn’t clarified whether the standard LPU will ship to Chinese buyers. Huang told CNBC in May that Nvidia had "largely conceded" China's AI chip market to Huawei.The Groq 3 LPU is built on Samsung's 4nm process with 512MB of SRAM per die and no HBM, and Nvidia said at GTC that it would ship in Q3 2026 to customers including OpenAI. U.S. export thresholds for China are set on compute density and bandwidth, and an SRAM-only decode accelerator with no HBM stack is the kind of part that can still be exported under them without a cut-down SKU, which is the mechanism The Information's sources described. ByteDance and Tencent each took delivery of roughly 10,000 H200s in recent weeks, according to a Financial Times report this week, the first meaningful Nvidia accelerator volume to enter mainland China since December's U.S. approval. items.titleZh: Nvidia denies report it will ship Groq-based LPUs to China by year-end — says there is 'no China-specific LPU product in our roadmap'
items.descriptionZh:
英伟达周四向Tom's Hardware发表声明，正式否认了有关其将为中国市场定制“语言处理单元”（LPU）并已接到多笔中国订单的报道。英伟达发言人表示：“The Information关于英伟达LPU的报道是错误的。我们今天在中国市场没有任何LPU销售，路线图中也没有针对中国的LPU产品。”这一回应明确否定了此前外界猜测英伟达正在为中国量身打造特供版AI推理芯片的说法。

被否定的报道源自科技媒体The Information，其引述了两名英伟达员工的说法，称英伟达计划在2026年底前向中国客户小批量出货一款LPU芯片，且已有数家中国企业下单。该报道指出，这款芯片是英伟达在2025年3月GTC大会上发布的Groq 3 LPU的变体，但硅片本身并未做任何改动，原因在于其硬件设计已经满足美国对华出口管制的要求。

要理解这一事件的来龙去脉，需要先弄清LPU的技术定位。Groq 3 LPU并非传统意义上的GPU，而是一种专门用于加速大语言模型解码（decode）阶段的协处理器。它基于三星4nm工艺制造，每个裸片集成512MB SRAM静态随机存取存储器，完全不使用HBM高带宽显存。这种架构使得整个加速器的计算密度和内存带宽特征与美国出口管制条例中针对中国设置的技术阈值并不冲突——美国限制的是高计算密度和极高带宽的芯片，而一个纯SRAM、无堆叠HBM的解码协处理器恰好落在可合法出口的范围内，因此英伟达无需额外开发缩减规格的SKU。

报道还披露了一个关键技术细节：LPU原本是英伟达下一代Vera Rubin平台的一部分，而Vera Rubin平台本身因性能过高无法对华销售。为了绕过这一限制，英伟达据称重写了负责GPU与LPU之间任务分配的软件层，使该加速器能够与在中国市场合法销售的处理器协同工作。换言之，英伟达试图通过软件层面的重新编排，让一款无法随原平台出口的硬件适配中国现有的合规计算生态。

然而，美国出口合规并不等于最终交付。报道也承认，即便英伟达完成技术适配，北京方面的态度依然不确定。中国官方去年曾明确阻止企业采购英伟达H20芯片，直到最近才松口允许部分H200进口——英伟达上个月刚刚获得向中国交付H200的许可。因此，即便芯片符合美国法规，中国政府的审批环节仍可能使交易流产。

值得注意的是，这不是英伟达首次被曝出准备为中国市场推出LPU。早在今年3月，就有传闻称英伟达正在为中国准备LPU，英伟达CEO黄仁勋当时在两天后回应称该消息“完全错误”。而周四这份声明的措辞比黄仁勋的坚决否认更收窄——它只强调“目前没有销售”和“没有中国特定产品”，却并未明确否认标准版LPU未来是否可能进入中国市场。英伟达没有就“标准LPU是否会向中国买家发货”这一问题作出澄清。

这一模糊态度背后，是英伟达在中国AI芯片市场日益尴尬的处境。黄仁勋今年5月接受CNBC采访时曾坦言，英伟达在中国AI芯片市场上“基本已经让位给了华为”。美国政府连续加码出口管制，使英伟达高端GPU无法进入全球最大的AI应用市场之一，而华为则借势推出了自研的昇腾系列芯片。

值得对比的是，The Information在报道中点名了LPU的直接竞争对手——华为昇腾950DT。这款芯片针对解码和训练任务进行了双重优化，预计2026年第四季度推出，而侧重预填充（prefill）阶段的昇腾950PR已于4月进入量产。华为正在以密集的产品节奏覆盖从训练到推理的完整链条，与英伟达形成正面竞争。

与此同时，中国互联网巨头也在政策变化中加速补货。据金融时报本周报道，字节跳动和腾讯在过去数周内各收到约一万块英伟达H200芯片，这是自去年12月美国批准对华出口以来，英伟达加速器首次大规模流入中国大陆市场。这一动向表明中国企业仍在积极寻求英伟达产品以维持算力竞争力，但供应量与中国庞大AI产业的实际需求相比仍显杯水车薪。

综合来看，英伟达此次否认LPU对华销售，既是对不实报道的澄清，也折射出在复杂的地缘政治背景下，这家芯片巨头在中国市场的每一步都面临双重监管的掣肘。技术本身是否具备合法性是一回事，能否真正落地又是另一回事。而无论英伟达未来是否推出针对中国的LPU，华为及其昇腾系列都已经牢牢占据了中国自主AI算力生态的核心位置，这场博弈远未结束。

The figure updates research DataDome published in March, which measured the ratio at about 6:1 across several e-commerce sites.Over the same period, the cheapest 128GB DDR5-6400 kit tracked by Tom's Hardware has reached $3,399, ten times its record low pricing. The Thales 2026 Bad Bot Report puts bad bots at 40% of all web traffic, less than half the share Segura reports on DDR5 listings.DataDome's March report documented a single operation that generated more than 10 million blocked requests, with a one-hour sample showing 91 DDR5 listings each polled around 551 times, or once every 6.5 seconds. The requests carried cache-busting parameters to defeat cached stock data and targeted industrial module makers such as Micron and Apacer, as well as DIMM socket suppliers Amphenol and TE Connectivity, alongside consumer brands.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Segura wrote on LinkedIn that retailers carrying memory should assume their "traffic analytics are probably understating the problem significantly." (Image credit: DataDome)Keep in mind that the 91% figure comes from one unnamed retailer, and DataDome hasn't published a sample window or its methodology. DataDome also sells the product that blocks this traffic, and page requests ultimately aren't purchases, so the ratio measures monitoring pressure on listings rather than how much stock bots actually end up securing, which can’t easily be quantified. Chang said in July that DRAM supply to independent module makers could fall to 30% of 2026 levels next year, and TrendForce expects conventional DRAM contract prices to rise another 13% to 18% in Q3 after roughly 60% in Q2. Hyperscale buyers have reportedly placed deposits against most of 2027's DRAM output.A 32GB DDR5-6000 kit that averaged $72 this time last year now averages $392 on PCPartPicker. While graphics card and console scalping in 2020 and 2021 ran against scheduled restocks that eventually outpaced resale demand, no equivalent restock date exists for consumer DDR5 before 2027 at the earliest.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsFramework stopped selling standalone RAM in November last year, citing scalpers, and Micro Center sells its CPU, motherboard, and 32GB DDR5 bundles in-store only with a one-per-household limit. Newegg and Amazon have run repeated CPU-plus-memory bundles that price a 32GB kit well below its standalone cost, which ties each kit to a processor a reseller then has to move as well. On eBay, we found G.Skill's Trident Z5 Neo 32GB kit listed at $836.54 in December against a $429.99 retail price, roughly double, and about seven times the $117.99 it sold for before the shortage. items.titleZh: DDR5 scalper bots now outnumber shoppers 10 to 1 — automated scraping hits listings every 6.5 seconds as 32GB kits surge from $72 to $392, DataDome researcher says
items.descriptionZh:
据DataDome威胁研究副总裁Jérôme Segura本周在LinkedIn上发布的消息，某零售商DDR5内存产品页面收到的流量中，恶意机器人（bad bots）占比高达91%，相当于每1次真人访问就有约10次自动请求。这一数字远超DataDome今年3月发布的约6:1的行业平均比例（该数据基于多个电商网站）。与此同时，Tom's Hardware追踪的最便宜128GB DDR5-6400套装价格已涨至3,399美元，是其历史最低记录的10倍。Thales《2026年恶意机器人报告》显示，全网流量中恶意机器人约占40%，远低于Segura在DDR5列表上观察到的份额。

DataDome在3月的报告中记录了一个单一操作，该操作生成了超过1,000万次被拦截的请求。在其中一小时采样中，91个DDR5商品列表每个被轮询约551次，平均每6.5秒一次。这些请求携带缓存破坏参数以绕过库存数据的缓存，目标不仅包括消费级品牌，还涉及美光（Micron）、Apacer等工业内存模组制造商，以及Amphenol和TE Connectivity等DIMM插槽供应商。Segura在帖子中写道，销售内存的零售商应意识到其“流量分析很可能严重低估了问题的规模”。

需要注意的是，91%这一数据来自一家未具名的零售商，DataDome未公布采样窗口或方法论。作为销售反机器人防护产品的厂商，DataDome自身也与此利益相关；此外，页面请求本身不等于实际购买，因此该比例更多反映的是监控压力，而非机器人最终抢到的库存数量——后者难以量化。

价格方面，32GB DDR5内存目前最低也要375美元。内存价格在12个月内飙升了500%，达到有追踪记录以来最低价的10倍。由于前所未有的内存短缺，DDR4内存和主板的生产已重新启动，PC行业正在为没有DDR5的世界做准备。Apacer首席执行官C.K. Chang在7月表示，明年独立模组制造商的DRAM供应可能降至2026年水平的30%。TrendForce预计，在第二季度合约价上涨约60%之后，第三季度常规DRAM合约价还将再涨13%至18%。据报道，超大规模买家已就2027年大部分DRAM产出支付了定金。去年同期均价72美元的32GB DDR5-6000套装，如今在PCPartPicker上均价已达392美元。

与2020至2021年显卡和游戏主机倒卖不同——当时有定期补货计划并最终超过转售需求——消费级DDR5在2027年之前不存在任何可预期的补货时间表。为此，Framework自去年11月起已停止单独销售内存；Micro Center仅限店内销售CPU、主板及32GB DDR5套装，且每户限购一套；Newegg和亚马逊则反复推出CPU+内存捆绑包，将32GB套装价格压到远低于单独购买的水平，但买家必须同时购买处理器，这迫使转售者不得不同时处理CPU。在eBay上，我们发现了G.Skill Trident Z5 Neo 32GB套装标价836.54美元，而其零售价为429.99美元，约为两倍，更是缺货前售价117.99美元的约七倍。

history.title: LG enters chip packaging arena with Laser Direct Imaging machine, as TSMC's CoWoS remains constrained — maskless machine is designed to pattern fine interconnects, trading resolution for higher throughput
history.description: LG rolls-out laser direct imaging lithography machine for chip packaging and high-density PCBs.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter As advanced packaging technologies like EMIB and CoWoS become yet another battlefield in the semiconductor industry, outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) companies are trying new tools in a bid to offer services that others do not. This week, LG Electronics Production Technology Institute (PRI) signed a contract with an OSAT to supply it with a maskless laser direct imaging (LDI) lithography tool that can be used to build metal-interconnect patterns in semiconductor packaging, potentially with higher yields than currently available tools, reports ETNews.LG-PRI's Laser Direct Imaging (LDI) system is a maskless lithography machine designed to pattern fine metal interconnects for advanced semiconductor packaging. While the company has developed various versions of the machine, its highest-resolution version can produce 1.5-µm line-and-space (L/S) patterns, which should be fine to 'print' wiring pitches of about 3 µm. The production equipment uses a 405-nm laser-diode light source and can process substrates as large as 600 × 600 mm, according to various media reports.LG positions its LDI system primarily for advanced semiconductor packaging using organic and then glass substrates, displays, and MEMS. Yet, it can also be used to build high-density printed circuit boards (PCBs) for mobile devices or prototype purposes.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: LG is entering an already established direct-imaging market led by KLA, Screen Holdings, Limata, and ORC, but participated in by a dozen manufacturers from Germany, France, Switzerland, Japan, and even China. What is notable is that LG is offering LDI systems with line/space capability down to 1.5-µm, which means it is targeting the higher end of the market. Yet, to establish a position, LG plans to price its LDI system competitively.Another way to pattern substratesThere are many ways to pattern substrates, including photolithography, e-beam lithography, nanoimprint lithography, and laser direct imaging, just to name a few. LDI is a maskless lithography process in which a laser exposes a digitally generated circuit pattern directly onto a photoresist-coated substrate, rather than transferring the pattern through a physical photomask. Instead of a photomask, an LDI system uses a digitally controlled pattern generator and projection optics, which resembles how a laser cinema projector projects a digital image onto a screen, except that LDI projects a circuit pattern onto photoresist. After development, the exposed resist leaves a pattern that defines where metal interconnects will be formed in later processing steps. You may like Intel's EMIB packaging gains traction as chip designers look beyond TSMC's constrained CoWoS TSMC says panel packaging won't replace CoWoS anytime soon for the largest future AI processors Chinese startup claims photonic chip production without DUV lithography, says nanoimprint process cuts costs by 90% (Image credit: LG)LG's LDI machine can produce down to 1.5-µm line-and-space patterns, which is good enough for chip substrates and even redistribution layers (TSMC CoWoS-R/-L uses RDL interposers with a minimum 4-µm pitch, or 2-µm line width/spacing). In contrast, competing products offer 1-µm, 3-µm, and 5-µm versions for different applications. While LDI in general cannot boast the resolutions offered by modern DUV, EUV, or e-beam lithography machines, LDI trades ultimate resolution for vastly higher throughput and large-area processing, exactly what the doctor ordered for production of PCBs or chip packaging. With current-generation LDI, the RDL interposer is the most advanced thing that these devices can pattern, as both CoWoS-S and CoWoS-L/EMIB-like technologies require considerably higher resolution. Meanwhile, there is another advantage that LDI machines have over lithography systems that rely on photomasks.Because the image is generated digitally, the system can create and calibrate patterns in real time, while projection optics, precision alignment, and stage control position the pattern accurately on the substrate. This capability is important because the dimensions/geometry of packaging substrates can vary and because organic substrates can expand, contract, or warp during processing. Given that we are talking about a 1.5-µm-scale wiring pattern, any shift from the nominal layout may result in a solder bridge or a faulty contact, which means yield loss. That said, the ability to adjust the pattern to the peculiarities of a substrate may be a game-changer for OSATs, their customers, and a major selling point for devices that can do it.A new kid on the block? Not reallyUnlike competing chaebols Samsung and SK Group, LG Group does not produce chips, even though its divisions supply various materials and components for the semiconductor industry. To that end, it is perfectly reasonable for the company to enter the market for tools for the production of chip packages or PCBs.In fact, LG PRI is not entering the exposure-equipment business from scratch. PRI traces its history to the Goldstar Production Technology Research Institute, established in 1987, and has worked on manufacturing and productivity technologies covering semiconductors, displays, and rechargeable batteries. Specifically, LG had already commercialized LDI technology for display manufacturing and supplied such equipment to LG Display.As a result, the semiconductor packaging-grade equipment represents an expansion of an existing LG technology into a new market rather than the development of an entirely new exposure platform from scratch and without any experience. Interestingly, LDI is the first element of LG's semiconductor equipment ambitions. The company reportedly plans to expand its portfolio into high-bandwidth memory (HBM) inspection equipment as well as through-glass-via (TGV) laser systems for glass substrates.ProspectsBefore LG expands to inspection or laser drilling tools, it will have to establish itself as a producer of reliable tools used for chip packaging, which will likely take years. For now, the significance of the deal with the undisclosed OSAT is less about business and more about the fact that an OSAT decided to give LG's LDI machine a try. Moving from university R&D installations to an OSAT mass-production facility provides LG a starting point for pursuing additional external orders.Whether LG can establish itself alongside Applied Materials, ORC, or Screen will depend on how its equipment performs in production and whether its emphasis on competitive pricing proves sufficient to persuade more packaging companies to adopt the system.In any case, a new Wafer Fab Equipment player is here, which is good news considering shortages of virtually all chipmaking tools. While LG's entrance will hardly have any noticeable impact on the market for at least a couple of years, another supplier could eventually add much-needed capacity, increase competition, and give chipmakers and OSATs another source of advanced packaging equipment.

history.titleZh: LG enters chip packaging arena with Laser Direct Imaging machine, as TSMC's CoWoS remains constrained — maskless machine is designed to pattern fine interconnects, trading resolution for higher throughput
history.descriptionZh:
先进封装技术正成为半导体产业竞争的新战场。随着英特尔的EMIB和台积电的CoWoS等先进封装方案日益普及，委外封装测试（OSAT）厂商正在积极寻找差异化工具，以提供别家没有的服务。本周，LG电子生产技术研究院（PRI）与一家OSAT签署合同，将向其供应一台无掩模激光直接成像（LDI）光刻设备，用于在半导体封装中制作金属互连图案，并有望比现有设备实现更高良率。

LG PRI的LDI系统是一种无掩模光刻设备，专为先进半导体封装精细金属互连图案化而设计。该公司开发了多个版本，其中最高分辨率版本可产生1.5微米的线宽/间距（L/S）图形，足以“印刷”约3微米间距的布线。该生产设备采用405纳米激光二极管光源，可处理最大600×600毫米的基板。LG将该系统主要定位用于基于有机基板、未来将扩展至玻璃基板的先进封装，以及显示器和MEMS领域，同时也可用于制造高密度移动设备PCB或原型样品。

LDI是一种无掩模光刻工艺：激光器将数字生成的电路图形直接投射到涂有光刻胶的基板上，而无需通过物理光掩模转印图案。它采用数字控制的图形发生器与投影光学元件，工作原理类似于激光影院投影仪将数字图像投射到屏幕上，只不过LDI投射的是电路图形到光刻胶上。显影后，光刻胶留下的图案定义了后续金属互连的形成位置。由于图像是数字生成的，系统可实时创建和校准图形，同时通过投影光学、精密对准和载台控制将图案准确位置于基板上。这一能力至关重要，因为封装基板的尺寸/几何形状可能变化，且有机基板在加工过程中会膨胀、收缩或翘曲。当涉及1.5微米级布线图案时，任何与名义布局的偏移都可能导致焊桥或接触不良，造成良率损失。因此，根据基板特性调整图案的能力可能成为OSAT及其客户的游戏规则改变者，也是具备此功能设备的一大卖点。

就分辨率而言，LDI无法与现代DUV、EUV或电子束光刻机相提并论，但它的取舍在于以极限分辨率为代价换取极高的生产效率和大幅面处理能力，这正是PCB或芯片封装生产所需要的。然而，LDI设备的另一个优势是：它可以不需要光掩模，直接数字生成并校准图形，还能适应基板的形变，这对先进封装尤其有价值。就当前代LDI而言，RDL中介层是这类设备能图案化的最先进产品——因为CoWoS-S和CoWoS-L/EMIB类技术需要高得多的分辨率。但LG的1.5微米L/S能力足以应对芯片基板甚至再分布层（TSMC CoWoS-R/-L采用最小4微米间距，即2微米线宽/间距的RDL中介层）。相比之下，竞争对手提供1微米、3微米和5微米版本以适应不同应用。

LG进入的是一个已由KLA、Screen Holdings、Limata和ORC主导的直接成像市场，参与者还包括来自德国、法国、瑞士、日本乃至中国的十余家制造商。值得关注的是，LG提供线宽/间距低至1.5微米的LDI系统，表明其瞄准市场高端。但为了建立地位，LG计划将LDI系统定在具有竞争力的价格。该技术的核心卖点之一是能处理有机基板在加工中的膨胀、收缩和翘曲，因为LDI可动态调整图案，避免因基板变形导致的良率损失。

LG集团与竞争对手三星、SK集团不同，不生产芯片，但其部门为半导体行业供应各种材料和组件。因此，进入芯片封装或PCB生产设备市场是完全合理的。事实上，LG PRI并非从零起步进入曝光设备领域。PRI的历史可追溯至1987年成立的金星生产技术研究院，长期研究涵盖半导体、显示器和可充电电池的生产与制造技术。具体而言，LG此前已将LDI技术商业化用于显示制造，并向LG Display供应此类设备。因此，半导体封装级设备是LG既有技术向新市场的扩展，而非毫无经验地开发全新曝光平台。有趣的是，LDI是LG半导体设备雄心的第一步，据报道该公司计划将产品组合扩展至高带宽内存（HBM）检测设备以及用于玻璃基板的玻璃通孔（TGV）激光系统。

在LG扩展到检测或激光钻孔工具之前，它必须首先确立自己作为可靠的芯片封装工具生产商的地位，这可能需要数年时间。目前，与未具名OSAT达成的协议，其意义与其说在于商业层面，不如说在于一家OSAT决定试用LG的LDI设备。从大学研发装置走向OSAT量产工厂，为LG提供了争取更多外部订单的起点。LG能否在应用材料（Applied Materials）、ORC或Screen等厂商面前立足，取决于其设备在生产中的表现，以及其强调的有竞争力的定价是否足以说服更多封装企业采用该系统。无论如何，一家新的晶圆厂设备（WFE）参与者出现了——考虑到几乎所有芯片制造工具都短缺，这无疑是好消息。尽管LG的进入在至少两年内不会对市场产生明显影响，但最终，新的供应商可能增加急需的产能、提升竞争，并为芯片制造商和OSAT提供另一个先进封装设备来源。事实上，这篇文章本身来自Tom's Hardware，其中还提到Intel的EMIB封装正在获得更多关注，而TSMC的CoWoS产能受限，以及一家中国初创公司声称无需DUV光刻即可生产光子芯片等等，这些都构成了先进封装设备需求旺盛的背景。LG的LDI设备以其1.5微米L/S能力、数字无掩模技术、实时校准和适应基板变形的能力，为高端封装市场带来了新选择，同时其竞争性定价策略和从显示器LDI延伸而来的技术积累，使其在市场中具有潜力。未来能否在先进封装设备领域站稳脚跟，将取决于实际量产表现和客户接受度。

history.title: Supermicro fires several employees following investigation into $2.5 billion China AI chip smuggling — claims that senior management had no knowledge of illicit transactions
history.description: An independent investigation on Supermicro clears senior management from any wrong-doing and also says that its financial statements were still reliable, despite the alleged diversion of its restricted products. Nevertheless, some of its employees from sales, technical support, and business development departments were fired for failing to 'follow Company policies or the Company’s code of conduct.'
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Five months after the arrest of Supermicro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw and two other co-conspirators for the alleged smuggling of Nvidia hardware into China, the company announced that it has completed its independent investigation and released its findings to the public, resulting in the termination of several employees. Supermicro said that the investigation, which was handled by an external law firm and conducted by an “independent forensic accounting consultant,” finds that neither the company nor its current senior executives were part of the alleged AI chip smuggling. It also said that it’s adopting all the recommendations to enhance its export compliance programs, although it did not directly admit that it was lacking in that department.Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explained“The investigation team reviewed the customer transactions that were the subject of the federal indictment, as well as transactions with a selection of other customers who bought restricted products, and did not find any evidence that any current member of senior management had knowledge of the alleged diversion scheme or of any actual diversion of restricted products by the Company,” Supermicro said in the statement. It also added, “The Company’s compliance personnel have acted in good faith, with the support of management, to mitigate the risk of the Company’s products subject to export controls being diverted to restricted parties or locations.”This odyssey began in March when the U.S. charged Liaw alongside Supermicro sales manager Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang and third-party broker Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun with conspiracy to unlawfully divert cutting-edge U.S. artificial intelligence technology to China. The accused aren’t operating a small-time smuggling operation, either — reports estimate that the three have smuggled hardware worth $2.5 billion since 2024. That massive amount has got shareholders worried that a huge chunk of the company’s sales come from illicit sales, resulting in some investors suing the company for securities fraud. Because of this, the company’s independent advisors also looked into this issue and said that it “did not find any evidence that the Company’s previously issued financial statements could not be relied upon based on the potential diversion of restricted products.”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Even though the third-party investigation exonerated Supermicro’s senior executives, it also resulted in the termination of several employees. The affected people were from the sales, technical support, and business development departments, although they were fired for breaking the company’s policies and code of conduct — the company said these moves were made "in connection with the investigation." Notably, none of the personnel were from its compliance department, and it’s also unclear how many people were dismissed.Supermicro also said that it’s enhancing its export compliance program, which Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said it must fix. Even though the company was never accused of wrongdoing and wasn’t part of the defendants in the case against the alleged smugglers, the fact that some of its employees were able to run a massive diversion scheme right within the organization raises major questions about the effectiveness of its compliance department. It said that it has already made changes that were recommended by its General Counsel and Chief Compliance Officer even before the third-party investigation concluded, and that its independent directors “will oversee implementation of the remaining recommendations.” You may like After $2.5 billion Supermicro smuggling bust, Nvidia CEO urges company to fix export control compliance Supermicro says it assisted Taiwanese authorities in server smuggling bust that led to three arrests Nvidia employee implicated in escalating AI GPU smuggling scandal The high demand for AI chips in China has meant the smuggling operations are quite lucrative, even as the U.S. is tightening its grip on export controls and Chinese authorities are commanding that its tech companies prioritize locally made Chinese chips instead of American AI GPUs. Nevertheless, the race to build ever more powerful AI models means that there is such a massive demand for the most advanced AI GPUs from Nvidia that some people are looking for ways to circumvent these bans and make “easy” money. history.titleZh: Supermicro fires several employees following investigation into $2.5 billion China AI chip smuggling — claims that senior management had no knowledge of illicit transactions
history.descriptionZh:
在Supermicro联合创始人Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw 与另外两名同伙因涉嫌向中国走私Nvidia硬件而被捕五个月后，该公司正式宣布其独立调查已告完成，并公开了调查结果。此次调查由外部律师事务所主导，并由独立法务会计顾问具体执行。Supermicro在声明中强调，调查未发现公司或其现任高级管理人员参与了这起所谓的AI芯片走私案，同时表示将采纳所有建议以强化出口合规计划，尽管并未直接承认此前在合规方面存在不足。

这起事件的源头可追溯至今年3月，美国司法部对Liaw、Supermicro销售经理Ruei-Tsang "Steven" Chang以及第三方中介Ting-Wei "Willy" Sun提起指控，罪名是共谋将美国尖端人工智能技术非法转移至中国。值得注意的是，这并非小规模的地下走私——据估算，自2024年以来，三人所走私的硬件总价值高达25亿美元。这一惊人金额引发了股东对该公司大量销售可能源于非法交易的担忧，进而导致部分投资者以证券欺诈为由将公司告上法庭。为此，公司独立顾问也对此进行了审查，并明确表示“未发现任何证据表明，基于受限产品潜在转移问题，公司此前发布的财务报表不可信赖”。

调查团队重点审查了联邦起诉书所涉的客户交易，以及一批购买受限产品的其他客户交易记录。Supermicro在声明中指出，调查未发现任何现任高级管理人员知晓所谓“转移计划”或公司实际将受限产品转移他处的证据。同时，公司合规人员在管理层的支持下一直秉持善意行事，以降低出口管制产品被转移到受限方或受限地点的风险。

尽管第三方调查为高管层洗清了嫌疑，但调查结果仍导致多名员工被解雇。这些被解雇人员来自销售、技术支持及业务发展部门，原因是违反公司政策和行为准则，公司称此举与“调查相关”。值得注意的是，被解雇人员中没有一名来自合规部门，且公司未透露具体解雇人数。Supermicro还表示正在加强出口合规计划——而这一点正是Nvidia首席执行官黄仁勋此前明确要求其必须修复的。尽管Supermicro本身从未被指控有不当行为，也未在该走私案中被列为被告，但员工能在组织内部运作如此大规模的转移计划，已经让外界对其合规部门实际效力产生了重大质疑。公司透露，早在第三方调查结束前，总法律顾问和首席合规官所建议的部分改革措施已开始实施，独立董事也将负责监督其余建议的落实。

这一事件折射出更宏观的行业背景：中国对AI芯片的需求极其旺盛，尽管美国不断收紧出口管制，且中国官方强制要求国内科技公司优先采购本土芯片而非美国AI GPU，但快速迭代的大模型竞赛使得最先进的Nvidia AI GPU仍然存在巨大缺口，这为走私者提供了绕开禁令牟取暴利的空间。此次调查虽然为Supermicro高管层化解了法律风险，但如何真正堵住合规漏洞，仍是这家服务器制造商乃至整个行业必须面对的长期挑战。

history.title: H200 AI GPUs finally reach China under case-by-case import licenses, but it's already too late for Nvidia — homemade chips corner the China market as country seeks semiconductor independence
history.description: Most of each company's U.S.-licensed allowance, understood to be up to 100,000 units apiece, must stay outside the mainland.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter ByteDance and Tencent each took delivery of roughly 10,000 Nvidia H200 accelerators in recent weeks, and a handful of other Chinese tech groups may soon receive approvals of similar size. The deliveries are the first meaningful movement of the chips into mainland China since President Trump cleared their export in December, but they arrive under strict oversight from China’s National Development and Reform Commission, which approves each purchase individually.Most of each company's U.S.-licensed allowance, understood to be up to 100,000 units apiece, must stay outside the mainland, largely in Hong Kong. Measured against the 400,000-plus units that ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent were collectively approved to buy in January, the chips now on the mainland amount to roughly 2.5% of the order book.Two licensing regimesTrump approved H200 exports in December last year, in exchange for a 25% cut of every sale to the U.S. Treasury, and terms formalized in January require each chip to pass through US territory for third-party inspection before re-export. The Commerce Department moved license applications to case-by-case review on January 16 and had cleared roughly 10 firms by mid-May, including Alibaba, ByteDance, Tencent, and JD.com, with Lenovo and Foxconn approved as distributors.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: In response, China built the NDRC’s per-purchase approval process from scratch to mirror the Commerce Department’s case-by-case license review. The 10,000-unit mainland allocations function as quantity caps, the very instrument that U.S. export rules have used since the first Hopper restrictions in 2022. The requirement to route imports via Hong Kong operates as an end-location condition, identical to Washington's demand that every chip transit U.S. soil for inspection.The Cyberspace Administration of China summoned Nvidia last July over alleged backdoors in the H20. State media outlets subsequently ran a campaign calling the chip unsafe and outdated, and state-funded data centers were barred from foreign accelerators. Eight months of NDRC silence on H200 orders left Jensen Huang telling investors Nvidia's China market share had gone from 95% to zero. You may like First Nvidia H200 shipments reach China, ByteDance and Tencent take deliveries as Beijing loosens its import block US allows Chinese telecom giant ZTE to purchase Nvidia H200 AI chips US closes loophole that allowed Chinese-owned subsidiaries located outside China to buy AI chips DeepSeek’s training bottleneckA transcript of DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng's May 20 closed-door investor meeting, leaked online in July, arguably explains why Beijing is letting any Nvidia silicon in at all. According to the document, whose authenticity DeepSeek hasn't confirmed, Liang told investors he wanted 200,000 Huawei accelerators to train a frontier model and received an allocation of 16,000, against total Huawei capacity of roughly 750,000 chips this year split across every Chinese AI company, a constraint he reportedly expected to persist for around three years. The remarks circulated widely enough that DeepSeek paused a fundraising round targeting a roughly $71 billion valuation days after they appeared.If we look at DeepSeek’s production history, it appears to match the numbers Liang cited during the meeting. lab's attempts to train its R2 model on Huawei Ascend hardware failed repeatedly, and training moved back to Nvidia chips while Ascend accelerators handle inference. Per the Financial Times’ unnamed source, which broke the story of resuming H200 imports, domestic silicon increasingly serves inference, while Nvidia hardware still carries training.The H200 obviously fills that gap nicely, with each unit carrying 141GB of HBM3e at 4.8 TB/s, delivering roughly six times the performance of the H20, and approaching the banned H100. A 10,000-GPU cluster is genuine frontier-training capacity, comparable to the builds behind the GPT-4 generation, though it represents a fraction of the 100,000-GPU-plus systems U.S. labs now run. That ratio seems to have been precisely calibrated by Beijing officials, large enough to keep flagship labs training their models, but small enough that inference stays a captive market for domestic chipmakers.Domestic supply gapsTrendForce's August 10 supply chain survey projects that domestic chips will take nearly 90% of China's high-end AI chip market this year, with domestic high-end shipments growing 83% year over year, a projection that TrendForce itself revised up from roughly 50% in its December outlook. Bernstein has recorded the same displacement from the other direction, with Nvidia's China share falling from 66% in 2024 to 40% in 2025 and a projected 8% this year.Huawei planned to roughly double output of its 910C Ascend chip to about 600,000 units in 2026, against a total Chinese accelerator market that ran to roughly 4 million units in 2025, 2.36 million of them supplied by Nvidia and AMD. So, while domestic chips can cover the volume, they can't yet cover frontier training, making the 90% projection and H200 easing two halves of the same policy.Washington's case for export controls rests on exactly the dependence these deliveries demonstrate: Four years into the restrictions, China's leading labs still can't train frontier models without American silicon, and Beijing has now conceded as much through its licensing decision.The leaked transcript has Liang arguing that open access to Nvidia would make domestic substitution a much harder commercial proposition, meaning the controls themselves built the market Huawei and Cambricon now hold, and TrendForce's numbers show that market approaching 90% share three years after the first Hopper bans. This month's deliveries disprove neither side's theory, but Nvidia does bear the cost of both, with 500,000 chips reportedly in inventory, a 25% fee on anything that sells, and a Chinese market rationed to 10,000 units per buyer — admittedly, that’s better than zero.
history.author: Luke James
history.titleZh: H200 AI GPU终于通过逐案进口许可进入中国，但对英伟达来说已为时过晚——随着中国寻求半导体独立，国产芯片已抢占中国市场
history.descriptionZh:
字节跳动与腾讯近日各收到约1万块英伟达H200加速器，这是自去年12月特朗普政府批准该芯片对华出口以来，首批大规模进入中国大陆的英伟达高端AI芯片。据悉，阿里、京东等中国科技集团也可能很快获得类似规模的审批。每家公司获批的芯片总量上限据称可达10万块，但绝大多数必须存放于境外（主要是香港），真正进入大陆的配额仅为总量的约四分之一。与今年1月字节跳动、阿里、腾讯合计获批的40余万块订单相比，此次实际交付仅占订单量的约2.5%。

这批芯片的放行背后是中美两套高度对称的许可制度。美方出口条件包括：每笔销售需向美国财政部缴纳25%的提成，且每颗芯片必须过境美国本土接受第三方检查后方可转口；商务部自1月16日起改为逐案审查，已在5月中旬前批准约10家企业，联想和富士康则获批为分销商。作为回应，中国发改委从零搭建了逐笔采购审批流程，将1万块大陆配额作为数量上限，并强制要求经香港转运，这恰好对应了美国自2022年首轮Hopper限制以来惯用的数量管控与终端位置条款。

此前，中国对英伟达芯片的态度一度十分严厉。去年7月，国家网信办曾就H20芯片涉嫌存在后门召见英伟达，官媒随后发起宣传攻势称该芯片不安全且过时，国有数据中心被明令禁止采购外国加速器。发改委对H200订单长达八个月的沉默，曾让黄仁勋向投资者坦言，英伟达在中国市场的份额已从95%降至零。

此次政策转向的直接动因，很可能是中国头部AI实验室在国产芯片上的训练困境。一份据称是DeepSeek创始人梁文锋5月20日闭门投资者会议的纪要（真实性未获官方确认）显示，他曾申请20万块华为昇腾加速器用于训练前沿模型，实际仅获得1.6万块的配额——华为当年的总产能约75万块，需分配给所有中国AI公司，这一瓶颈预计将持续三年。该纪要流传后，DeepSeek一度暂停了估值约710亿美元的融资。从DeepSeek的生产实践来看，其R2模型在昇腾硬件上多次训练失败，不得不转回英伟达芯片，昇腾仅承担推理任务，这与外媒“国产芯片主推理、英伟达主训练”的报道相吻合。

H200恰好填补了这一空缺。每块H200配备141GB HBM3e高带宽内存，带宽达4.8TB/s，性能约为此前特供中国的H20的六倍，接近被禁的H100。一个由1万块H200组成的集群，已具备训练GPT-4一代模型的真实前沿算力，但与美国实验室普遍拥有的10万卡级系统相比仍有量级差距。这一比例显然是北京方面精算的结果：足以让头部实验室继续训练模型，又不足以让推理市场脱离国产芯片的“圈养”，从而为华为昇腾、寒武纪等本土厂商保留核心市场空间。

TrendForce于8月10日发布的供应链调查预计，国产芯片今年将占据中国高端AI芯片市场近90%的份额，高端出货量同比增长83%——该机构已在去年12月约50%的预测基础上大幅上调。Bernstein的数据从另一角度印证了同样的趋势：英伟达在华份额已从2024年的66%降至2025年的40%，预计今年仅剩8%。华为计划在2026年将其910C昇腾芯片产量翻倍至约60万块；而2025年中国加速器市场总量约400万块，其中236万块来自英伟达和AMD。数字表明，国产芯片虽可覆盖规模需求，却仍无法支撑前沿训练，90%的国产化预测与H200的有限放行，本质上是同一政策的两面。

华盛顿坚持出口管制的理由，恰好被这批交付所证实：限制实施四年后，中国顶尖实验室依然离不开美国芯片来训练前沿模型，北京通过许可决定承认了这一点。而泄露的纪要中梁文锋的观点则指出了另一面——若无美国芯片的开放供应，国产替代的商业动力将大幅削弱，正是出口管制“帮助”华为和寒武纪建立了今天的市场。TrendForce的数据显示，管制三年后国产份额已逼近90%，也印证了这一逻辑。本月这批交付无法最终裁决谁的理论更正确，但英伟达显然为此付出双重代价：据传其积压库存达50万块，任何在售芯片都要上交25%的利润，而中国大陆市场被限额在每个买家1万块——不过，对英伟达来说，这终究好过销量为零。

history.title: Nvidia denies report it will ship Groq-based LPUs to China by year-end — says there is 'no China-specific LPU product in our roadmap'
history.description: Nvidia has rejected a report published by The Information that it plans to begin small-batch shipments of an LPU tailored for Chinese customers by the end of 2026.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia has rejected a report claiming that it plans to begin small-batch shipments of a language processing unit tailored for Chinese customers by the end of 2026, with several Chinese orders already placed. "The reporting in The Information on NVIDIA's LPU is incorrect. We have no LPU sales in the China market today, and no China-specific LPU product in our roadmap," an Nvidia spokesperson told Tom's Hardware on Thursday. The Information's story, which cited two Nvidia employees, said the chip is a variant of the Groq 3 LPU Nvidia announced at GTC in March, and that its silicon is unchanged because it already falls within U.S. export rules.Tom's Hardware Premium Roadmaps (Image credit: Future)Leading-edge foundry roadmapsNvidia Enterprise GPU and CPU roadmapAMD's Enterprise GPU and CPU roadmapIntel's roadmaps examined — 14A, Nova Lake, Diamond Rapids & AI accelerator pushCo-Packaged Optics (CPO) foundry roadmapsThe LPU was designed as a decode co-processor for the Vera Rubin platform, and Vera Rubin can't be sold in China. The Information's sources said Nvidia rewrote the software that splits work between the GPU and the LPU so the accelerator can run alongside processors that are available in the country.The publication said Nvidia didn't respond to requests for comment over several days before publishing, and that it's unclear whether Beijing would allow the orders to proceed. Chinese officials blocked purchases of the H20 last year and only recently told companies they'd permit some H200 imports, so U.S. compliance alone doesn't guarantee the chips can be delivered.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Back in March, it was reported that Nvidia was preparing LPUs for China, with Jensen Huang saying two days later that the story was "totally false.” Thursday's statement is narrower than Huang's, addressing current sales and a China-specific product. Nvidia hasn’t clarified whether the standard LPU will ship to Chinese buyers. Huang told CNBC in May that Nvidia had "largely conceded" China's AI chip market to Huawei.The Groq 3 LPU is built on Samsung's 4nm process with 512MB of SRAM per die and no HBM, and Nvidia said at GTC that it would ship in Q3 2026 to customers including OpenAI. U.S. export thresholds for China are set on compute density and bandwidth, and an SRAM-only decode accelerator with no HBM stack is the kind of part that can still be exported under them without a cut-down SKU, which is the mechanism The Information's sources described. history.titleZh: Nvidia denies report it will ship Groq-based LPUs to China by year-end — says there is 'no China-specific LPU product in our roadmap'
history.descriptionZh:
英伟达周四向Tom's Hardware发表声明，正式否认了有关其将为中国市场定制“语言处理单元”（LPU）并已接到多笔中国订单的报道。英伟达发言人表示：“The Information关于英伟达LPU的报道是错误的。我们今天在中国市场没有任何LPU销售，路线图中也没有针对中国的LPU产品。”这一回应明确否定了此前外界猜测英伟达正在为中国量身打造特供版AI推理芯片的说法。

被否定的报道源自科技媒体The Information，其引述了两名英伟达员工的说法，称英伟达计划在2026年底前向中国客户小批量出货一款LPU芯片，且已有数家中国企业下单。该报道指出，这款芯片是英伟达在2025年3月GTC大会上发布的Groq 3 LPU的变体，但硅片本身并未做任何改动，原因在于其硬件设计已经满足美国对华出口管制的要求。

要理解这一事件的来龙去脉，需要先弄清LPU的技术定位。Groq 3 LPU并非传统意义上的GPU，而是一种专门用于加速大语言模型解码（decode）阶段的协处理器。它基于三星4nm工艺制造，每个裸片集成512MB SRAM静态随机存取存储器，完全不使用HBM高带宽显存。这种架构使得整个加速器的计算密度和内存带宽特征与美国出口管制条例中针对中国设置的技术阈值并不冲突——美国限制的是高计算密度和极高带宽的芯片，而一个纯SRAM、无堆叠HBM的解码协处理器恰好落在可合法出口的范围内，因此英伟达无需额外开发缩减规格的SKU。

报道还披露了一个关键技术细节：LPU原本是英伟达下一代Vera Rubin平台的一部分，而Vera Rubin平台本身因性能过高无法对华销售。为了绕过这一限制，英伟达据称重写了负责GPU与LPU之间任务分配的软件层，使该加速器能够与在中国市场合法销售的处理器协同工作。换言之，英伟达试图通过软件层面的重新编排，让一款无法随原平台出口的硬件适配中国现有的合规计算生态。

然而，美国出口合规并不等于最终交付。报道也承认，即便英伟达完成技术适配，北京方面的态度依然不确定。中国官方去年曾明确阻止企业采购英伟达H20芯片，直到最近才松口允许部分H200进口——英伟达上个月刚刚获得向中国交付H200的许可。因此，即便芯片符合美国法规，中国政府的审批环节仍可能使交易流产。

值得注意的是，这不是英伟达首次被曝出准备为中国市场推出LPU。早在今年3月，就有传闻称英伟达正在为中国准备LPU，英伟达CEO黄仁勋当时在两天后回应称该消息“完全错误”。而周四这份声明的措辞比黄仁勋的坚决否认更收窄——它只强调“目前没有销售”和“没有中国特定产品”，却并未明确否认标准版LPU未来是否可能进入中国市场。英伟达没有就“标准LPU是否会向中国买家发货”这一问题作出澄清。

这一模糊态度背后，是英伟达在中国AI芯片市场日益尴尬的处境。黄仁勋今年5月接受CNBC采访时曾坦言，英伟达在中国AI芯片市场上“基本已经让位给了华为”。美国政府连续加码出口管制，使英伟达高端GPU无法进入全球最大的AI应用市场之一，而华为则借势推出了自研的昇腾系列芯片。

值得对比的是，The Information在报道中点名了LPU的直接竞争对手——华为昇腾950DT。这款芯片针对解码和训练任务进行了双重优化，预计2026年第四季度推出，而侧重预填充（prefill）阶段的昇腾950PR已于4月进入量产。华为正在以密集的产品节奏覆盖从训练到推理的完整链条，与英伟达形成正面竞争。

与此同时，中国互联网巨头也在政策变化中加速补货。据金融时报本周报道，字节跳动和腾讯在过去数周内各收到约一万块英伟达H200芯片，这是自去年12月美国批准对华出口以来，英伟达加速器首次大规模流入中国大陆市场。这一动向表明中国企业仍在积极寻求英伟达产品以维持算力竞争力，但供应量与中国庞大AI产业的实际需求相比仍显杯水车薪。

综合来看，英伟达此次否认LPU对华销售，既是对不实报道的澄清，也折射出在复杂的地缘政治背景下，这家芯片巨头在中国市场的每一步都面临双重监管的掣肘。技术本身是否具备合法性是一回事，能否真正落地又是另一回事。而无论英伟达未来是否推出针对中国的LPU，华为及其昇腾系列都已经牢牢占据了中国自主AI算力生态的核心位置，这场博弈远未结束。

history.title: DDR5 scalper bots now outnumber shoppers 10 to 1 — automated scraping hits listings every 6.5 seconds as 32GB kits surge from $72 to $392, DataDome researcher says
history.description: Bad bots account for 91% of the traffic reaching one retailer's DDR5 memory product pages, roughly 10 automated requests for every legitimate visit.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 5 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Bad bots account for 91% of the traffic reaching one retailer's DDR5 memory product pages, roughly 10 automated requests for every legitimate visit, according to a LinkedIn post this week from Jérôme Segura, VP of threat research at bot-mitigation firm DataDome. The figure updates research DataDome published in March, which measured the ratio at about 6:1 across several e-commerce sites.Over the same period, the cheapest 128GB DDR5-6400 kit tracked by Tom's Hardware has reached $3,399, ten times its record low pricing. The Thales 2026 Bad Bot Report puts bad bots at 40% of all web traffic, less than half the share Segura reports on DDR5 listings.DataDome's March report documented a single operation that generated more than 10 million blocked requests, with a one-hour sample showing 91 DDR5 listings each polled around 551 times, or once every 6.5 seconds. The requests carried cache-busting parameters to defeat cached stock data and targeted industrial module makers such as Micron and Apacer, as well as DIMM socket suppliers Amphenol and TE Connectivity, alongside consumer brands.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Segura wrote on LinkedIn that retailers carrying memory should assume their "traffic analytics are probably understating the problem significantly." (Image credit: DataDome)Keep in mind that the 91% figure comes from one unnamed retailer, and DataDome hasn't published a sample window or its methodology. DataDome also sells the product that blocks this traffic, and page requests ultimately aren't purchases, so the ratio measures monitoring pressure on listings rather than how much stock bots actually end up securing, which can’t easily be quantified. You may like 32GB of DDR5 now costs $375 minimum Memory prices climb 500% in 12 months, up to 10x the lowest ever tracked prices Production of DDR4 memory and motherboards is restarting amid unprecedented memory shortages — PC industry preparing for a world without DDR5 Apacer CEO C.K. Chang said in July that DRAM supply to independent module makers could fall to 30% of 2026 levels next year, and TrendForce expects conventional DRAM contract prices to rise another 13% to 18% in Q3 after roughly 60% in Q2. Hyperscale buyers have reportedly placed deposits against most of 2027's DRAM output.A 32GB DDR5-6000 kit that averaged $72 this time last year now averages $392 on PCPartPicker. While graphics card and console scalping in 2020 and 2021 ran against scheduled restocks that eventually outpaced resale demand, no equivalent restock date exists for consumer DDR5 before 2027 at the earliest.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsFramework stopped selling standalone RAM in November last year, citing scalpers, and Micro Center sells its CPU, motherboard, and 32GB DDR5 bundles in-store only with a one-per-household limit. Newegg and Amazon have run repeated CPU-plus-memory bundles that price a 32GB kit well below its standalone cost, which ties each kit to a processor a reseller then has to move as well. On eBay, we found G.Skill's Trident Z5 Neo 32GB kit listed at $836.54 in December against a $429.99 retail price, roughly double, and about seven times the $117.99 it sold for before the shortage. history.titleZh: DDR5 scalper bots now outnumber shoppers 10 to 1 — automated scraping hits listings every 6.5 seconds as 32GB kits surge from $72 to $392, DataDome researcher says
history.descriptionZh:
据DataDome威胁研究副总裁Jérôme Segura本周在LinkedIn上发布的消息，某零售商DDR5内存产品页面收到的流量中，恶意机器人（bad bots）占比高达91%，相当于每1次真人访问就有约10次自动请求。这一数字远超DataDome今年3月发布的约6:1的行业平均比例（该数据基于多个电商网站）。与此同时，Tom's Hardware追踪的最便宜128GB DDR5-6400套装价格已涨至3,399美元，是其历史最低记录的10倍。Thales《2026年恶意机器人报告》显示，全网流量中恶意机器人约占40%，远低于Segura在DDR5列表上观察到的份额。

DataDome在3月的报告中记录了一个单一操作，该操作生成了超过1,000万次被拦截的请求。在其中一小时采样中，91个DDR5商品列表每个被轮询约551次，平均每6.5秒一次。这些请求携带缓存破坏参数以绕过库存数据的缓存，目标不仅包括消费级品牌，还涉及美光（Micron）、Apacer等工业内存模组制造商，以及Amphenol和TE Connectivity等DIMM插槽供应商。Segura在帖子中写道，销售内存的零售商应意识到其“流量分析很可能严重低估了问题的规模”。

需要注意的是，91%这一数据来自一家未具名的零售商，DataDome未公布采样窗口或方法论。作为销售反机器人防护产品的厂商，DataDome自身也与此利益相关；此外，页面请求本身不等于实际购买，因此该比例更多反映的是监控压力，而非机器人最终抢到的库存数量——后者难以量化。

价格方面，32GB DDR5内存目前最低也要375美元。内存价格在12个月内飙升了500%，达到有追踪记录以来最低价的10倍。由于前所未有的内存短缺，DDR4内存和主板的生产已重新启动，PC行业正在为没有DDR5的世界做准备。Apacer首席执行官C.K. Chang在7月表示，明年独立模组制造商的DRAM供应可能降至2026年水平的30%。TrendForce预计，在第二季度合约价上涨约60%之后，第三季度常规DRAM合约价还将再涨13%至18%。据报道，超大规模买家已就2027年大部分DRAM产出支付了定金。去年同期均价72美元的32GB DDR5-6000套装，如今在PCPartPicker上均价已达392美元。

与2020至2021年显卡和游戏主机倒卖不同——当时有定期补货计划并最终超过转售需求——消费级DDR5在2027年之前不存在任何可预期的补货时间表。为此，Framework自去年11月起已停止单独销售内存；Micro Center仅限店内销售CPU、主板及32GB DDR5套装，且每户限购一套；Newegg和亚马逊则反复推出CPU+内存捆绑包，将32GB套装价格压到远低于单独购买的水平，但买家必须同时购买处理器，这迫使转售者不得不同时处理CPU。在eBay上，我们发现了G.Skill Trident Z5 Neo 32GB套装标价836.54美元，而其零售价为429.99美元，约为两倍，更是缺货前售价117.99美元的约七倍。
